questions.solution:
The magnetic dipole moment of a revolving electron: The electron of change (–e) performs uniforms circular motion around a stationary heavy nucleus of charge +Ze. This constitutes a current I.

  ∴ I= e T ...(i)

Where, T is the time period of revolution. Let r be the orbital radius of electron and v the orbital speed. Then

  T= 2πr υ ...(ii)

Substituting the value of T in (i), we get

  I= e 2πr υ = eυ 2πr

The magnetic moment (m) associated with this circular current is

  m=Iπ r 2 [ ∵ m → =I A → ]

  ∴ m= eυ 2πr ⋅π r 2 = eυr 2

or F ∝ σ 2 R 2 ε 0

questions.q: A magnetic needle free to rotate in a horizontal plane is placed at the centre of a circular current-carrying coil whose axis is perpendicular to the magnetic meridian at that place. It is also known that the magnetic declination at this place is zero and in this condition, the magnetic needle is pointing towards the north-west. Now, if we reverse the direction of current in the coil, then the magnetic needle will
questions.solution: If there is no current in the coil, then the needle would point north but due to the magnetic field of the coil, it is pointing north-west. This means the magnetic field due to the coil is towards west and it is equal to the horizontal component of earth's magnetic field. So when we reverse the direction of current the magnetic field due to the coil will be towards east and the magnetic needle will point north-east.

questions.q: Which of these materials requires the least value of magnetic field strength to magnetize it?
questions.solution:
The least value of magnetic field strength required to magnetize is nickel because it is a ferromagnetic material. Ni is a ferromagnetic substance which gets strongly magnetized when placed in an external magnetic field. When external magnetic field B0, is applied the magnetic domains orient themselves in the direction of magnetic filed and grow in size.

Hence, Ni requires least value of magnetic strength. NaCl is a diamagnetic material. Its field lines are repelled.

If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> are the net magnetic fields due to the earth at the two places respectively, then the ratio <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is approximately equal to
questions.solution:
Let f1 and f2 be the respective oscillation frequencies respectively for 45° and 30° dip. Then,

f1=12πMB1cos45°I

f2=12πMB2cos30°I

f1f2=B1cos45°B2cos30°

⇒302402=B1cos45°B2cos30° 

⇒B1B2=900×cos30°1600×cos45°

⇒B1B2=0.688≈0.7

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ferromagnetic material is heated above its curie temperature. Which one of the following is the correct statement?
options: Ferromagnetic material changes into diamagnetic material
questions.solution: Beyond curie temperature, ferromagnetic material turns into paramagnetic material, as if ferromagnetic domains become random.

What is the ratio of magnetic moments?
questions.solution:
Here we use sum and difference method.

M2M1=T22-T12T22+T12

Where T1 and T2 are time periods

T ∝1n (∵n is frequency.)

⇒ M1M2=n12 + n22n12 - n22

=122+42122-42=144+16144-16=108=1.25

questions.q: The magnetic susceptibility of a material of a rod is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>499</mn></math>. The absolute permeability of vacuum is<math><mi> </mi><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H </mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. questions.solution:
Absolute permeability of material of rod

μ=μrμ0=1+Xmμ0

∴ μ=1+499×4π×10-7=2π×10-4 H m-1

∴ μ0 M=5×10-5 Wb-m

M=5×10-5μ0Am2

Also, B=8π×10-4=μ0H

∴ H=8π×10-4μ0

T=2πIMH

I=MHT24π2=5×10-5×8π×10-4×1524π2μ02

=5×10-5×8π×10-4×2254π24π×10-72

I=2250×10-9π(16π2)×10-14=4.54×105 kg m2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A hoop and a solid cylinder of same mass and radius are made of a permanent magnetic material with their respective axes. But the magnetic moment of hoop is twice of solid cylinder. They are placed in a uniform magnetic field in such a manner that their magnetic moments make a small angle with the field. If the oscillation periods of hoop and cylinder are <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></math> respectively, then:
questions.solution:
Time period of any magnetic body place in an external magnetic field is:-

T=2πIMB

Thoop=2πmR2MB ...... (1) Ihoop=mR2

Tc=2πmR22M2B  ...... (2) ISolid cylinder=mR22

From (1) and (2)

Th=Tc

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic needle of a vibration magnetometer makes 12 oscillations per minute in the horizontal component of earth's magnetic field. When an external short bar magnet is placed at some distance along the axis of the needle in the same line, it makes 15 oscillations per minute. If the poles of the bar magnet are interchanged, the number of oscillations it makes per minute is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>n</mi></msqrt></math>. What is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>?
questions.solution:
Ist case :

n=12πMBHI

⇒ n∝BH ⇒ n1n2=BHBH+BH1

⇒ 1215=BHBH+BH1

⇒ BH1=916BH

IInd case :

        n2n3=BH+BH1BH-BH1

⇒ 15n3=BH+916BHBH-916BH

∴    n3=63⇒n=63
